title.en: Practical 10: Identification of adaptations in plants

text.en: A cactus, a water hyacinth and a pitcher plant solve survival in very different ways.

The aim is to identify plant specimens and list their adaptations. The specimens are a mesophytic plant (tomato or brinjal), a xerophytic plant (Opuntia), an aquatic plant (Eichhornia) and an insectivorous plant (Nepenthes).
Observe each plant and note the features that suit its habitat, for example the thick fleshy stem of Opuntia that stores water, the floating leaves of Eichhornia and the pitcher of Nepenthes that traps insects.
Write these adaptations as numbered points in your record.
